title: Jonah and the Winter
premise: Petra Yarrow, a rationalist pest controller, is hired to clear Winterhallow House, where the last resident—an elderly woman named Maren—must sign inheritance papers before the estate can pass to the family. But the house's mirrors lag a second behind reality, and the lag is growing, revealing a thing with fingerprints that wears the faces of everyone who ever lived there. The house is sustained by a lullaby whose final verse was never written down; whoever sings it whole inherits the house, and whatever lives inside it. Petra must learn the verse from Maren without ever singing along, keep her own reflection from learning her face, and choose between the truth of what the family did generations ago and the loyalty Maren asks of her. In the end, Petra refuses to sing, helps Maren finish the verse alone as she dies, and signs nothing—leaving the house to collapse inward on its own reflection, taking the thing with fingerprints with it.
about_author: O. M. Ravensworth is the pen name of a former building surveyor who spent a decade inspecting derelict properties across the north of England and never once went into an empty house's attic without checking the mirrors first. They write horror about paperwork, inheritance, and the terrible arithmetic of old families.

chapters.title: The Callout
chapters.summary: Petra Yarrow takes a pest control job at Winterhallow House: scratching in the walls, the client says, something with fingerprints. Petra, who believes in rats and dry rot and nothing else, arrives to find the house immaculate and cold. POV: Petra. Beat: confident skepticism meeting the first wrong detail—a child's handprint on the inside of a sealed attic door.

chapters.title: Mrs. Maren Voss
chapters.summary: Petra meets the last resident, Maren Voss, ninety-one, sharp as a tack, who insists the scratching is 'just the house remembering.' A lawyer's letter on the table: inheritance papers awaiting signature. Maren asks Petra, oddly, whether she can carry a tune. POV: Petra. Beat: unease disguised as professional courtesy; the reader senses Maren knows more than she says.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: Petra works the walls, finds no droppings, no nests, no entry points. In the hallway mirror she raises her hand; her reflection follows—visibly, measurably, a second late. She times it against her watch three times before she stops timing it. POV: Petra. Beat: the rationalist's first crack, played as procedural horror rather than panic.

chapters.title: The Family Tree
chapters.summary: Petra researches the Voss family at the county archive and finds a pattern: every generation, one member 'stays on' at Winterhallow and dies there, while the rest scatter and prosper. The house has never been sold. It has only ever been signed over. POV: Petra. Beat: dread through paperwork; the inheritance theme takes root.

chapters.title: What the Walls Are Made Of
chapters.summary: Back at the house, Petra opens a wall cavity and finds it packed with hair, fingernail parings, and handwritten scraps of a lullaby—all verses but the last. The scratching stops whenever she touches them. POV: Petra, with an interlude from Maren's 1963 diary. Beat: the horror becomes tactile and domestic; the song enters the story.

chapters.title: The Verse That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Maren admits the family lullaby kept 'the resident' asleep for two hundred years, but the final verse died with her grandmother, who sang it into her ear as a child—too young to remember it whole. Without it, the papers can't be signed, and the thing wakes fully. POV: Maren. Beat: the rules of the world established; Maren's fear is for Petra, not herself.

chapters.title: Fingerprints
chapters.summary: Petra dusts the attic door and lifts prints that match no living person—then matches one to a photograph of Maren's brother, dead sixty years. The prints are fresh. POV: Petra. Beat: the title creature announces itself; skepticism is now a liability, and Petra knows it.

chapters.title: The Lag Widens
chapters.summary: The mirrors now lag three seconds. Petra watches her reflection finish an action she hasn't started, and understands it is practicing being her. She covers every mirror in the house with bedsheets. POV: Petra. Beat: the enemy acquires a strategy; identity becomes the battlefield.

chapters.title: The Nephew Arrives
chapters.summary: Daniel Voss, the heir, arrives to hurry the signing, all charm and impatience. He dismisses the scratching, mocks the covered mirrors, and hums the lullaby's known verses absently at dinner. The house responds: every door in the wing opens at once. POV: Daniel. Beat: a new threat—loyalty to family vs. truth of the house; Daniel wants his inheritance and doesn't care what comes with it.

chapters.title: What Daniel Signed
chapters.summary: Petra finds a draft of the inheritance deed with a clause in faded ink: the signatory assumes 'all obligations, resident and otherwise.' Daniel has already signed a preliminary acceptance to unlock the estate's funds. The lag in the mirrors now shows a second Petra, standing slightly wrong. POV: Petra. Beat: the trap closes; loyalty and greed are revealed as two doors into the same room.

chapters.title: The Brother in the Attic
chapters.summary: Maren confesses: the resident is her brother Tomas, who 'stayed on' in 1954, and the thing with fingerprints wears him like a coat. The lullaby doesn't banish it—it keeps the wearer dreaming so the house can pretend he's only sleeping. POV: Maren. Beat: the horror acquires a human face and a grief at its center; loyalty vs. truth becomes personal.

chapters.title: Petra Sings
chapters.summary: Exhausted, Petra catches herself humming the verses she's read on the wall scraps—and her reflection hums back, in harmony, a half-second early. She stops. Her reflection doesn't, for eleven full seconds. POV: Petra. Beat: the midpoint reversal; Petra has broken her own first rule, and the house knows her voice now.

chapters.title: The Archive of Faces
chapters.summary: Petra breaks into the sealed attic and finds a nursery of mirrors, each etched with a name: every family member who ever 'signed.' In the oldest glass, something moves that is not her reflection. It has her hands. POV: Petra. Beat: full revelation of the house's mechanism; the inheritance is the feeding.

chapters.title: Daniel's Night
chapters.summary: Daniel, alone in the guest wing, follows humming into the hall of mirrors to see 'his family.' He meets a reflection of himself that knows things he hasn't done yet, and comes back down changed—politer, slower, blinking a beat behind the world. POV: Daniel. Beat: the cost of disloyalty to the truth; the house begins wearing him.

chapters.title: The Grandmother's Tape
chapters.summary: Petra finds a reel-to-reel recording in Maren's room: her grandmother singing the lullaby, and the tape degrades precisely at the final verse—eaten, Maren says, 'by the house, so no one could learn it and leave.' But under the hiss, Petra hears a second voice. Tomas's. Singing along. POV: Petra. Beat: hope with a hook in it; the last verse exists in only one living memory.

chapters.title: The Choice of Maren Voss
chapters.summary: Maren offers Petra a way out: leave tonight, never come back, let the house take Daniel and then Maren, and it will sleep again for another generation. Petra, who has never believed and now cannot stop, refuses to leave her. POV: alternating. Beat: the loyalty vs. truth theme crystallizes; both women choose each other over safety.

chapters.title: What the House Wants Sung
chapters.summary: The house stops hiding. Walls breathe; the wallpaper shows handprints surfacing like drowned things. The thing with fingerprints walks the halls wearing Tomas's face, then Daniel's, then—briefly, horribly—Petra's mother's. It is teaching her the last verse, note by note, wanting her to sing it herself. POV: Petra. Beat: rising climax; the trap revealed—the verse can only be learned by singing along.

chapters.title: The Papers
chapters.summary: Daniel, mostly worn, presents the deed for signature, his reflection standing beside him with the pen already moving. Petra realizes signing is the same as singing: either act completes the inheritance. She burns the deed in the kitchen stove, and the house screams through every mirror at once. POV: Daniel, then Petra. Beat: climax begins; the paperwork and the song are one mechanism.

chapters.title: The Last Verse
chapters.summary: Maren, dying, takes Petra's hands and sings the final verse into her ear as her grandmother did—but Petra holds the song in her mouth like a stone, never letting her voice join, never letting her reflection hear it whole. Maren finishes alone. The mirrors stop lagging. Then they shatter, one by one, from the attic down. POV: Petra. Beat: the climax; the rule kept at the cost of everything.

chapters.title: Tomas
chapters.summary: With the song finished by its last true resident, the house releases what it wore: for one minute, in the last unbroken mirror, Petra sees Tomas Voss as a boy of nineteen, tired and grateful, before the glass goes dark and stays dark. Maren dies holding her brother's name like a finished sentence. POV: Petra. Beat: grief and release; the horror resolves into mourning.

chapters.title: Sign Nothing
chapters.summary: Petra signs the completion paperwork for the pest control job—nothing else—and walks out of Winterhallow as it folds inward on its own dark mirrors, quietly, like a house exhaling. Daniel, half-worn, watches from the gate and doesn't follow. The inheritance passes to no one. POV: Petra. Beat: resolution; refusal as victory.

chapters.title: The Song in the Walls
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Petra takes a routine callout to a flat across town. In the bathroom mirror, her reflection is exactly on time. But as she packs up her tools, she catches herself humming a tune she never learned all the way through—and stops, deliberately, before the last verse. POV: Petra. Beat: coda; the inheritance of memory can't be fully refused, only declined daily.
